campaigns.body:
For the metaverse gallery hosted on Spatial.io, a scavenger hunt game was designed to encourage visitor engagement. Small 3D objects were installed within the artwork with hyperlinks that redirected visitors to google forms. These objects were blended within the artwork to prevent the hunt from being too easy since the gallery space is relatively compact. Once a participant finds an image code, they will be prompted to take a screenshot and submit it via the YIF email or Instagram DM to earn a price.The google forms had questions where the visitors were required to solve ESG related questions, fulfilling the goal of education while also keeping them interactive. 

The scavenger hunt will run for two full months, providing visitors enough time to participate. After the event ends, a prize draw will be conducted. The winner is distributed into 4 categories: one participant will receive the first prize, three will receive second prize, six will receive third prize, and ten participants will receive participation rewards. For google forms, the players’ score would determine their prize tier.

The first prize will be a gift card valued at over 10,000₩, such as a Starbucks or convenience store gifticon. The second prize will consist of a gifticon around 5,000₩ while the third prize will be around 2,000₩. All participants who complete the challenge but do not win a major prize will receive an ESG-themed NFT. This approach ensures that everyone receives a reward for participating. 

To advertise the metaverse and keep engagement high, the scavenger hunt will be promoted primarily through Instagram and YouTube. Instagram Reels and Youtube shorts will help gain more exposure, promoting prize reveals. There will also be videos that will explain how to participate in the hunt and how to apply to win a prize. Threads may also be used to post updates during the campaign.

In addition to the scavenger hunt, we are creating and selling merchandise based on our ESG themed NFT artwork. The production and sales will be designed through Marpple Shop – a website that allows users to upload custom designs and sell them– with features such as international shipping  making the goods accessible to a global audience. 

The goods will incorporate the designs of the ESG-themed NFTs and will be categorised into two main types. First, there are practical ESG goods – tumblers, eco-bags, and mugs — items that align with the environmental aspect of ESG by promoting reusable alternatives. Second, there are smaller collectible items – stickers, keyrings, phone grips, and custom-wrapped chocolates.

campaigns.summary: 제안 정책/법안 요점 및 핵심: 1) 기업이 핵심 사업부를 물적분할한 뒤 자회사를 상장하는 방식(이중상장)은 소액주주의 권익을 침해하고, 모회사 주가 하락을 유발함. 2) 물적분할은 '중대한 경영 결정'으로 보고, 반드시 주주총회 특별결의를 통해 진행. 3) 물적분할 엄격한 심사를 통한 승인 및 기존 모회사 일반주주 신주 우선 배정. 4) 제도 개선을 통해 소액주주의 의결권 보장 및 기업에 대한 신뢰 회복 유도...
campaigns.body:
[b]제안 정책/법안 요점 및 핵심[/b]
[ul][li]기업이 핵심 사업부를 물적분할한 뒤 자회사를 상장하는 방식(이중상장)은 소액주주의 권익을 침해하고, 모회사 주가 하락을 유발함[/li]
[li]물적분할은 '중대한 경영 결정'으로 보고, 반드시 주주총회 특별결의를 통해 진행[/li]
[li]물적분할 엄격한 심사를 통한 승인 및 기존 모회사 일반주주 신주 우선 배정[/li]
[li]제도 개선을 통해 소액주주의 의결권 보장 및 기업에 대한 신뢰 회복 유도[/li][/ul]

[b]제안 정책/법안의 필요성 및 세부 내용[/b]
[b]문제점:[/b]
[ul][li]현행법상 물적분할은 이사회 결의만으로 가능하며, 자회사의 상장 역시 제한이 없어 소액주주가 배제된 채 가치가 외부로 이전됨[/li]
[li]대표 사례: LG화학은 배터리 부문을 물적분할하고, 100% 자회사인 LG에너지솔루션을 상장했으며 이로 인해 LG화학의 주가는 약 800,000원에서 223,000원으로 급락[/li]
[li]소액주주는 LG에너지솔루션 지분을 받지 못한 채 손실만 떠안음[/li][/ul]

[b]제안 내용:[/b]
[b]물적분할 시 주주총회 특별결의 의무화[/b]
[ul][li]전체 주주의 ⅔ 이상 또는 소액주주 10% 이상 동의 요건[/li]
[li]대주주가 과반을 점유한 상황에서도 형식적 결의 방지[/li][/ul]

[b]회사 쪼개기 상장 심사 강화 및 소액주주 보호[/b]
[ul][li]물적분할 후 일정 기간(예: 3년) 이내 자회사 상장 제한[/li]
[li]상장이 필요할 경우 금융당국의 사전 심사 및 주주 보호 대책 의무화[/li]
[li]쪼개기 상장 시 모회사 소액 주주에게 보상 신주 우선배정[/li][/ul]

[b]주요 참고 사례[/b]
[ul][li]메리츠금융: 자회사 상장폐지 + 대주주 지분 희생 → 주가 3.5배 상승[/li]
[li]LG화학: 물적분할 후 이중상장 → 주가 급락, 소액주주 피해[/li][/ul]


[b]예상 소요예산[/b]
법령 개정 및 감독 강화를 위한 행정 비용 중심. 별도 예산은 크지 않음


[b]제안 정책/법안의 차별성 및 기대효과[/b]
[b]차별성:[/b]
[ul][li]기존 제도는 기업의 결정권만 보장, 본 제안은 [b]소액주주의 동의권과 보호조치 명문화[/b][/li]
[li]법적 의무화를 통해 기업의 자율 규범 수준을 제도화[/li]
[li]메리츠 사례처럼 [b]주주 친화적 지배구조[/b]로 전환하는 구조 제시[/li][/ul]

[b]기대효과:[/b]
[ul][li]소액주주의 실질적 권리 보장[/li]
[li]주가 하락에 따른 투자 불신 해소[/li]
[li]ESG 관점에서 기업의 ‘G(Governance)’ 강화[/li]
[li]자본시장의 장기 신뢰 회복과 투자 활성화[/li][/ul]

campaigns.title: Petition for Victoria's Secret to Stop Promoting Unrealistic Beauty Standards
campaigns.author: Youth Impact Fund
campaigns.summary: Victoria’s Secret has advocated unrealistic and misleading beauty standards and body images, lacking the inclusion of plus-size models and promoting the concept of “The Perfect Body.” This has contributed to causing mental health problems, including depression, eating disorders, and even suicidal thoughts, particularly influential for teenagers...
campaigns.body:
[b]Petition Summary[/b]

Victoria’s Secret has advocated unrealistic and misleading beauty standards and body images, lacking the inclusion of plus-size models and promoting the concept of “The Perfect Body.” This has contributed to causing mental health problems, including depression, eating disorders, and even suicidal thoughts, particularly influential for teenagers. We, the Youth Impact Fund, initiate a call for Victoria’s Secret to embrace diverse sizes of models on runways and foster the wording that supports self-love and true beauty. The Youth Impact Fund demands your signature on this petition for changes that extend beyond Victoria’s Secret to protect the teenagers by redefining beauty and body image and meeting global ESG goals. 


[b]Who we are[/b]

Youth Impact Fund [url]www.youthimpact.com[/url] is the world’s first youth-managed fund pursuing global ESG goals. We manage a $100,000 valued investment portfolio, actively considering environmental, social, and governance factors to aim for better performances of corporations regarding their social responsibility. The Youth Impact Fund has launched a campaign against Victoria’s Secret to address the failure to include diverse sizes of models and destructive influences generated by their false marketing choices. 


[b]The issue[/b]

Victoria’s Secret has contributed to shaping the standard of ‘ideal beauty’ for a long time, which is closely tied with mental health problems and body image issues for people, particularly for females in the younger generation. It has consistently advocated unrealistic beauty standards while lacking diversity and inclusion, promoting ‘perfect bodies’ and exposing models who are mostly white in its runway. While Victoria’s Secret has made attempts to undertake the issues, problems have not been adequately addressed since it fails to eliminate deep-rooted exclusion in its brand. It is crucial to understand the problems and pursue measurable changes that reflect true diversity and empower people of all shapes, sizes, races, and identities. 

Victoria’s Secret includes models increasingly thinner over 23 fashion shows. According to the study From Angels to #Real Women published in Spring 2020 (Kennedy), a total of 54 models appeared in Victoria's Secret’s 50 sample posts, and 88.9% (48) of them were categorized as wearing small size, 7.4% (4) as medium size, and 3.7% (2) of models as large size. It indicates that the average size of Victoria’s Secret’s models is far smaller than the national average size of women, 16-18, which is considered as women’s plus size 20W. Victoria’s Secret’s promotion of the concept of ‘The Perfect Body' deteriorates people’s perception of their own bodies, causing serious problems that are difficult to address at once. Mental Health Foundation has reported that 31% of teenagers and 35% of adults feel depressed or ashamed of their body image. Exposure to television, social media, and film influences the formation of their body images. Stricter standards of beauty and the use of unrealistic body images can lead individuals to feel deep dissatisfaction with their own body images, increasing the chance of mental health struggles, including low self-esteem, depression, shame and anxiety, eating disorders, and even suicidal thoughts (French). Indeed, according to the 2017 Dove Global Girls Beauty and Confidence Report, 52% of 1000 survey participants aged 10-17 answered that toxic beauty contents cause low self-esteem (Dove). In essence, Victoria’s Secret’s contents, including the concept of “The Perfect Body,” have developed these detrimental mental health problems resulting from negative body image by twisting the idea of “real beauty.” 


[b]Our Demands[/b]

It is a crucial responsibility for brands like Victoria’s Secret to be part of those who initiate inclusivity in the fashion industry. We sincerely call on Victoria’s Secret to increase the representation of models of all sizes. That is, inclusion of plus-size models is essential. According to the data provided by social commerce platform Mys Tyler, 54.4% of American women wear clothing size plus-size (CSA). Notwithstanding the reality, fashion brands, particularly on their runways, overlook the large portion of plus-size women, and it is reasonable that we request Victoria’s Secret to feature at least 10% of plus-size models to reflect on realistic distribution of clothing sizes. In addition to this, Victoria’s Secret must ensure diverse sizes of models are not portrayed differently from each other. 

Furthermore, extreme words like “The Perfect Body” easily lead to biased standards of beauty and body image, instigating mental health problems, which are major concerns that it must address. We request Victoria’s Secret to acknowledge the harm induced by their past word choices in advertisements and instead increase the use of words fostering self-love, individuality, and body positivity. 


[b]Why Your Signature Matters[/b]

In fact, overweight or underweight teenagers (determined by the actual measurement of height and weight) have merely slightly more suicidal tendencies than teenagers of normal weight (CBS). Yet, suicidal thoughts or attempts of 13,601 teenagers in 9th to 12th grade whose own body perception was extreme (either fat or skinny), which they believed was varied from ‘the standard’ developed by society, were more than twice as prevalent as those who did not perceive their body image as extreme (CBS). The study indicates that body image matters for young teenagers, underscoring that negative body image undoubtedly not only gives rise to the mental disorders but also to suicidal attempts. We urge you to take action by signing this petition to stop intensifying the problem and support teenagers suffering from mental disorders engendered by misled standards and body images. While this campaign is directed at Victoria’s Secret, the Youth Impact Fund aims to spread further impacts in the fashion industry, providing the opening of true inclusion based on earnest consideration of diverse sizes, races, and genders of models. We endeavor to raise awareness of mental health problems caused by unrealistic beauty standards and body image issues due to underrepresentation of diverse body sizes. Addressing social issues in advocacy of ESG principles starts with your signature, your contribution. By participating in this campaign, you advance to take the essential step of the change for protecting young teenagers, demanding true inclusivity, and redefining beauty in a way that uplifts individuals.

campaigns.title: Stop Amazon’s harsh working conditions that increase injury rates
campaigns.author: Youth Impact Fund
campaigns.summary: Amazon consistently ranks among the top companies with the highest worker injury rates. Employees are subjected to relentless labor with minimal rest, lifting heavy loads under extreme time constraints. As a result, the Youth Impact Fund has launched this petition to advocate for better working conditions and to reduce Amazon’s alarming injury rates...
campaigns.body:
[b]Petition Summary[/b]

Amazon consistently ranks among the top companies with the highest worker injury rates. Employees are subjected to relentless labor with minimal rest, lifting heavy loads under extreme time constraints. As a result, the Youth Impact Fund has launched this petition to advocate for better working conditions and to reduce Amazon’s alarming injury rates.


[b]Who We Are[/b]

The Youth Impact Fund is a group dedicated to addressing corporate issues, particularly those related to ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) violations. We started this initiative after witnessing numerous instances of ESG violations and recognizing the urgent need for change. Our goal is to protect Amazon workers and employees in similar industries from hazardous working conditions that put them at high risk of injury.


[b]The Issue[/b]

The primary issue is the high injury rate at Amazon warehouses. Amazon has 30 percent more workplace injuries compared to other e-commerce and shipping companies like Target and FedEx. These injuries severely impact workers' physical and mental well-being, often pushing them to go on strike, as seen in the past.

Additionally, Amazon has repeatedly violated workers’ rights by exposing warehouse employees to dangerous conditions that lead to low back injuries, musculoskeletal disorders, and other long-term health issues. Workers are overworked in hazardous environments with minimal safety precautions.

Another critical issue is poor worker selection and training. Many employees who are not physically prepared for heavy lifting are assigned to labor-intensive tasks, increasing the likelihood of injuries.

Moreover, seasonal work surges significantly worsen the situation. During peak periods such as Prime Day and holiday sales, workers experience excessive workloads, immense pressure, and insufficient rest, leading to even higher injury rates. However, instead of implementing protective measures, Amazon prioritizes profit over worker safety. According to OSHA investigators, Amazon warehouse workers are frequently exposed to high risks of back injuries and other musculoskeletal disorders.


[b]Our Demands[/b]

[b]Improved Warehouse Infrastructure & Worker Selection[/b]

Amazon must expand warehouse spaces to accommodate workers more safely and reduce congestion.

The company must revise its hiring process to ensure that individuals assigned to heavy lifting are properly trained and physically capable.

Amazon should increase the number of workers to distribute physical labor more effectively, reducing the risk of overexertion and workplace collisions.

[b]Reduced Pressure During Peak Sales Periods[/b]

Amazon must eliminate excessive pressure on workers during peak shopping seasons, including Prime Day, Black Friday, and the holiday season.

Workers should receive adequate breaks and reasonable work expectations to prevent exhaustion and injury.

In 2022, 10 percent of Amazon workers were injured during Prime Day. We demand that Amazon implement changes to reduce this injury rate to 4 percent this year.


[b]Why Your Signature Matters[/b]

Your signature is crucial in advocating for safer working conditions at Amazon. By signing this petition, you are helping:

[ul][li]Reduce the injury rate among Amazon workers[/li]
[li]Ensure a safer and fairer worker selection process[/li]
[li]Hold Amazon accountable for unethical labor practices[/li]
[li]Support workers who face unnecessary pressure during peak sales seasons[/li][/ul]

Let’s stand together for the well-being of Amazon’s workforce. Sign this petition and demand immediate action from Amazon.

campaigns.title: Request for Improved Working Conditions in Coupang's Logistics Centers
campaigns.author: Youth Impact Fund
campaigns.summary: All of Coupang’s logistics centers are built in a mezzanine structure, which divides a single floor into three. Notwithstanding the efficiency of the structure in storage, it deteriorates the working conditions for the laborers...
campaigns.body:
All of Coupang’s logistics centers are built in a mezzanine structure, which divides a single floor into three. Notwithstanding the efficiency of the structure in storage, it deteriorates the working conditions for the laborers. The greater number of floors allows the company to double or even triple the number of products stored, which eventually leads to an increase in the internal density of the logistic center. Such extremely high internal density not only increases the temperature and humidity but also disables proper ventilation, making those centers vulnerable to heatwaves during the summertime.

Concerning such vulnerable structures of Coupang’s logistics center, the Ministry of Employment and Labor compared Coupang Dongtan Logistics Center with the nearby GMarket Logistics Center and pointed out the following. Coupang has a mezzanine structure, but G Market has a single-story structure with a higher floor height, allowing for smoother air circulation. Moreover, although the mezzanine structure impedes airflow, fans installed indiscriminately without considering industrial ventilation in a center reduce the cooling effect.

Despite the vulnerability to heatwaves within Coupang’s logistics centers, a sufficient number of breaks are not guaranteed to the employees. In August 2023, Coupang’s temperature monitoring commission, which consists of actual employees, reported that the perceived temperature and humidity in Coupang’s logistic centers during the summertime are around 34°C and 58%, respectively. According to the Occupational Safety and Health Act, at a perceived temperature of 33°C, 10 minutes of break, and at a perceived temperature of 35°C, 15 minutes of break per hour are highly recommended to be provided. However, the commission reported that Coupang Logistics Centers do not guarantee break times in accordance with the heatwave warning recommended by the Ministry of Employment and Labor's guidelines. Moreover, they contended that Coupang Logistics Center determines whether break time is guaranteed based on the temperature and humidity of the time and location set by itself, rather than the time or location with the highest perceived temperature. In Coupang Daegu Center, for instance, workers on the 1.5 floor are working at a perceived temperature of 38°C. Furthermore, the commission disclosed that the company's headquarters are not taking any actions to equalize the break times for every center in different regions, and that break times differ by center, shift, and floor.

However, it is impossible to mandate logistics centers like Coupang to install cooling, heating, and ventilation facilities due to the absence of legal provisions. According to the Mechanical Equipment Act, buildings with a total floor area of 10,000 square meters or more must be equipped with heating, cooling, and ventilation facilities that meet certain standards.

“For buildings with a total floor area of 10,000 square meters (3,000 pyeong) or more, heating, cooling, and ventilation facilities must be confirmed to meet technical standards by the mayor or governor before construction begins, and they must undergo inspection before use after construction is completed.” Article 15 of the Mechanical Equipment Act and Article 11 of the Enforcement Decree.

However, Coupang’s logistics centers are an exception to the law. According to the Building Act's 'Types of Buildings by Use,' the Coupang Logistics Center (Logistics Terminal) is a warehouse rather than a building. Ultimately, according to the current law, the installation of air conditioning and ventilation facilities is at the discretion of the business owner, no matter how hot the logistics center is.

Hence, reflecting on the devastating working conditions of Coupang’s logistics center, the protection of workers must be enforced through not only legislation that goes beyond recommendations for measures against heatwaves but also alterations to the contemporary Mechanical Equipment Act.

In essence, Coupang's "Rocket Delivery" has propelled the corporation to a prominent position in the e-commerce industry by guaranteeing the arrival of the ordered product in less than a day. Yet, behind the scenes of the so-called “Rocket Delivery,” the corporation has infringed on the major Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG) principles, more specifically on the social aspect of it. Reflecting on its lack of commitment to the welfare of employees, this report calls for not only public attention to the issue but also immediate action for the enhancement of working conditions, aligned with ethical standards and legal requirements. Hence, the success story of Coupang must be evaluated not only by its market dominance but also by its commitment to the welfare of its employees.

campaigns.title: Request for Meta to Provide Transparency on Illegally Released User Data
campaigns.author: Youth Impact Fund
campaigns.summary: In recent times, Meta (formerly Facebook), the renowned U.S. social media giant, has been facing a series of formidable challenges, leading to significant fines and a sharp decline in stock prices...
campaigns.body:
In recent times, Meta (formerly Facebook), the renowned U.S. social media giant, has been facing a series of formidable challenges, leading to significant fines and a sharp decline in stock prices. The Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) took action against Meta, imposing a hefty fine of $275 million for their continued violations of European privacy regulations. The situation had worsened over time, with the cumulative fines reaching a staggering 912 million euros since the previous fall.

The violations that prompted such penalties were severe and concerning. Meta had engaged in unauthorized data scraping and mishandling of personal information, particularly on its subsidiary platform, Instagram. These actions culminated in one of the most substantial cases of GDPR violations ever recorded. To make matters worse, Meta's grandiose and ambitious investment in the Metaverse, highlighted by a name change to reflect their vision, had not yielded the expected results. The disappointment was palpable, resulting in a sharp decline in the company's stock prices and prompting the CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, to announce a series of massive layoffs.

In response to the mounting public outrage and regulatory scrutiny, the National Assembly convened a heated debate on the right to disagree, drawing in prominent lawyers from various organizations and representatives from the Justice Party. The focus of the debate centered on Meta's handling of user information and privacy concerns.

Amidst the growing opposition and mounting legal pressure, Meta was forced to postpone the implementation of its new personal information processing policy. This policy had sparked immense controversy as it required users to agree to share non-essential personal information for advertising and marketing purposes, raising valid concerns about user privacy and consent. Critics were quick to point out the problematic nature of Meta's use of personal information for customized advertisements, with particular concern over the company's uncertain control over user data even after obtaining consent. As a potential solution, they proposed introducing contextual advertisements as a more privacy-conscious alternative.

The critics' arguments were bolstered by the fact that such practices appeared to violate the Personal Information Act, which expressly prohibits service providers from refusing service based on users' refusal to provide non-essential personal information. The current information request by Meta was seen as excessive and potentially illegal, running afoul of the principles of minimum data collection and transparency, which the law aimed to protect.

Further fueling the controversy, the CEO of the Progressive Network Center came forward and revealed troubling findings. According to their investigations, Meta had been surreptitiously collecting personal information from users' external activities on Facebook without proper consent. This included details of users' interactions with partner websites and apps, raising serious concerns about unauthorized data distribution and the potential misuse of cookies for targeted advertising.

In light of the gravity of the situation, experts emphasized the need for robust legal and institutional measures to regulate social media platforms effectively. They argued that consumers must be provided with genuine choices when it comes to customized advertisements, ensuring that their privacy rights are upheld.

As a response to the mounting pressure and controversies surrounding Meta's data practices, the Personal Information Protection Committee launched a thorough investigation into the company's collection and handling of user data. The investigation aimed to ascertain whether Meta's collection of user data was genuinely essential for providing its services and whether any further violations had occurred.

In addition to the challenges and controversies mentioned earlier, Meta (formerly Facebook) faced further revelations concerning the infringement of users' personal information, leading to even more serious legal and public relations issues. It was disclosed that Meta had been surreptitiously collecting users' personal profiles, family and relationship/marriage status, education, and living place, without proper consent. This unauthorized data collection occurred through Facebook's third-party apps and services, exposing the personal information of millions of users without their knowledge or approval.

The situation in Korea mirrored the global concerns about Meta's data practices. In November 2020, the Korean Personal Information Protection Commission imposed a substantial penalty of KRW 6.7 billion on Meta for the unauthorized provision of personal information through Facebook's third-party apps. This penalty stemmed from the fact that Facebook, now Meta, had been illegally providing users' personal information to third-party app developers since 2007 through the Facebook Platform, violating privacy laws and regulations.

The investigation into Meta's activities revealed that not only did they share the personal information of users who had used the apps, but also the personal information of those users' friends, further compounding the breach of privacy. Despite making changes to their Graph API access in response to previous controversies, the unauthorized provision of personal information to third parties persisted until as late as June 2018, when the Cambridge Analytica scandal brought these practices to light.

As a result of these violations, the Korean Personal Information Protection Commission imposed fines and corrective measures on Meta. This included a surcharge of KRW 6.7 billion for the unauthorized provision of personal information, as well as additional fines for actions such as storing user passwords without encryption and submitting false data during the investigation. Despite the penalties and efforts by regulatory authorities, Meta's problems were not fully resolved, and the issue continued to escalate.

Youth Impact Fund (www.youthimpact.com) has recently launched a critical campaign targeting Meta, addressing their failure in upholding ESG principles. campaigns.title: Stop Altria's unethical marketing of Juul e-cigarettes to children
campaigns.author: Youth Impact Fund
campaigns.summary: Until 1954, when Scientists Cuyler Hammond and Daniel Horn discovered a cause-and-effect relationship between lung cancer and smoking, the general public was largely unaware of the negative effects of smoking (Mendes)...
campaigns.body:
Until 1954, when Scientists Cuyler Hammond and Daniel Horn discovered a cause-and-effect relationship between lung cancer and smoking, the general public was largely unaware of the negative effects of smoking (Mendes). As such, smoking was a societal norm for most of the 20th century, with “around half of the population of industrialized nations [smoking]” (Rodrigues) in the late 1950s. Taking advantage of its widespread popularity, Big Tobacco not only marketed its products to adults, but also to children. Ad campaigns such as the Smooth Joe ads, advertising the Camel brand of cigarettes, were targeted to “children and young adolescents” (Burns, etl). This advertising was deemed so harmful that even the United States Department of Justice sued “several major tobacco companies” for “[targeting] the youth” (Eubanks).

Fortunately, in today’s society, the problem of smoking has largely been alleviated with smoking rates declining since 1959 (Burns, etl). Whilst this harmful vice is meeting its slow end, in its demise, vaping has taken place. Vaping refers to the inhaling of “vapor created by an electronic cigarette”. While electronic cigarettes (e-cigs) have fashioned themselves as a healthier alternative to smoking, in reality, vaping is extremely harmful with it having been linked to “serious lung damage and even death” (Gordan).

Adding insult to injury, cigarette companies such as the Altria Group Inc., the parent company to Malbrough Cigarette, have managed to adapt to the current marketplace, becoming major stakeholders in the vaping industry themselves. With its acquisition of 35% of Juul Labs Inc., the largest vaping company in the world, Altria has become the largest shareholder of Juul. With this acquisition, Altria has managed to control Juul from the background with the former's own Chief Growth Officer, K.C Crosthwaite, being placed as Juul’s CEO. Altria's domination over Juul’s operations has led to the continuation of unethical practices by Big Tobacco with Altria bringing back old strategies, such as marketing to children, to Juul. For example, Juul has purchased ad space on several child-focused websites such as “Nickelodeon, the Cartoon Network, Seventeen magazine and educational sites for middle school and high school students” (Kaplan). Furthermore, Juul has also created fruit and candy-flavored e-cigarette flavors as these flavors were perceived as being less dangerous by the youth (British Medical Association). 

By not only buying up ad space on platforms where children commonly frequent but also by creating vaping flavors that appeal to and seem safer for teenagers to use, it is clear that Juul and its parent company, Altria, are marketing their product towards the youth population. As a result of this strategy, roughly 20% of high school students are reported to have vaped in the United States according to the Partnership to End Addiction. In 2018, the National Institute of Health also reported that 37.3 percent of 12th graders reported having used a vaping product in the past 12 months, compared to just 27.8 percent in 2017.

While it may be too hard to hold Juul and Atria legally accountable for their harmful marketing strategies and product, it is possible to spread awareness of their unethical business practices. Young students should not only be made aware of the extent to which vaping can harm them but also of how they have been lied to by Juul and Altria as e-cigarette flavors such as fruit or candy are dangerous despite the safe allure of these flavors. By spreading awareness of their unethical business practices, it may be possible to live in a future where children are no longer taken advantage of by vaping companies. 

The most effective strategy to get Juul to change its unethical marketing practices is to effect change from within. Recently, Engine No. 1, an investment firm creating long-term value and driving positive impact through active ownership, was able to impact real change in the energy company ExxonMobil, a company notorious for its disregard of the environment, by winning three seats on ExxonMobil’s board. They were able to do this, ironically, by becoming shareholders of ExxonMobil themselves and winning the support of major institutional investors and pension funds with large investments in the company, including CalPERS, CalSTRS, and New York State Common Retirement Fund. Taking advantage of the current ESG trend, Engine No. 1 was able to bring the oil giant to its knees by effecting change from the inside. Similarly, like Engine 1, we can pursue a similar course of action towards Altria. 

Recently, Youth Impact (www.youthimpactse.com) started its own campaign against Juul and Altria through the Youth Impact Fund. The Youth Impact Fund is the world’s first youth-managed social impact fund that uses environmental, social, and governance factors in deciding how its managers will invest $40,000. The Youth Impact Fund also tries to pressure global companies that go against today’s ESG trend and people’s expectations in terms of corporate social responsibility, by initiating various campaigns against the company. Like Engine No. 1, one strategy that the Youth Impact Fund uses is symbolically buying a share of the company it is campaigning against and, as a shareholder, rightfully demanding the company’s leadership to act in the best interest of its shareholders - specifically, to minimize long-term ESG risks, which has become more important than ever. 

The Youth Impact Fund has symbolically bought a share of Altria Group Inc. (NYSE: MO) to start a campaign objecting the company’s advertising of e-cigarettes to children through Juul, which Altria effectively has control over as the majority shareholder. Through this petition, the Youth Impact Fund aims to spread awareness about Altria's behind-the-scenes involvement in the vaping pandemic all over the world, and to mobilize support for the newly launched campaign. Please sign this petition to express your support for our campaign and to demand Altria to stop all marketing of Juul's e-cigarette products to children. The Youth Impact Fund will also send a copy of our petition and the signatures we receive to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which has the authority to reject Juul's application to continue marketing and selling highly addictive menthol-flavored and high-nicotine e-cigarettes.

sections.title: Investment Objectives
sections.body:
The purpose of my investment is not simply to earn money. Of course, financial return is important because investment should be economically meaningful. However, I also want my investment to reflect my values and beliefs.

By investing in a responsible construction company, I want to support businesses that improve society rather than harm it. Construction companies shape the spaces where people live, work, and build communities. Because of this, I believe they have a strong responsibility to protect workers, reduce environmental damage, and contribute to sustainable development.

This investment also helps me develop my own identity as an investor. Instead of choosing companies only because their stock prices may rise, I want to learn how to evaluate companies based on both financial performance and ethical responsibility. Through this process, I hope to become an investor who makes thoughtful decisions and supports companies that can create long-term positive impact.

In conclusion, my purpose is to invest in a company that can grow sustainably while respecting human safety, environmental protection, and financial responsibility. I believe this kind of investment is meaningful because it connects economic goals with social and environmental values.

sections.title: Investment Philosophy
sections.body:
My investment philosophy is based on the belief that companies should create value not only for shareholders, but also for workers, communities, and the environment. Since I am interested in investing in a construction company, I believe it is important to look beyond short-term profit and consider how the company operates in the real world.

First, I want to invest in companies that genuinely care about the [b]safety and well-being of construction workers.[/b] Construction is a physically demanding and sometimes dangerous industry, so a responsible company should prioritize worker protection, provide proper training, follow safety regulations, and prevent accidents as much as possible. A company that protects its workers is more likely to be ethical, stable, and respected in the long term.

Second, I want to invest in companies that use [b]sustainable construction materials[/b] and reduce environmental harm. Construction can cause pollution, waste, carbon emissions, and damage to natural spaces. Therefore, I believe construction companies should try to use eco-friendly materials, reduce waste, improve energy efficiency, and avoid unnecessary environmental destruction.

Third, I believe that a company should have [b]sustainable finance.[/b] This means that the company should not rely only on risky short-term profits, excessive debt, or environmentally harmful projects. Instead, it should maintain financial stability while investing in long-term innovation, worker safety, and environmental responsibility.

Overall, my investment philosophy is to support construction companies that balance [b]profit, people, and the planet.[/b] I believe that truly strong companies are not only financially successful but also socially responsible and environmentally sustainable.

sections.title: Investment Strategy
sections.body:
My investment strategy is to choose construction companies that can grow sustainably while protecting workers, reducing environmental harm, and maintaining financial stability. Since construction companies shape homes, workplaces, and cities, I believe they should be evaluated not only by profit, but also by their responsibility toward people and the environment.

First, I will focus on [b]worker safety.[/b] Construction is a dangerous industry, so I will prioritize companies that provide safety training, use accident-prevention systems, and protect workers on-site. Second, I will consider [b]environmental sustainability[/b], including the use of eco-friendly materials, waste reduction, pollution prevention, and energy efficiency. Third, I will examine [b]financial stability[/b], avoiding companies that depend too much on short-term profits, excessive debt, or risky projects.

Based on this strategy, companies such as [b]Samsung C&T, Hyundai E&C, Daewoo E&C, and DL E&C[/b] could be strong candidates. These companies show different strengths in worker safety, ESG disclosure, sustainability reporting, and green construction.

Overall, my strategy is to invest in construction companies that balance [b]profit, people, and the planet.[/b] This allows me to pursue financial return while supporting companies that create long-term positive impact.

[li]Commercial aviation recovery and fleet modernization[/li]

By doing so, the fund seeks to minimize the risks that are specific to the industry and benefit from the latest technologies in defense systems, such as AI-based defense systems, electronic warfare, and advanced materials in aerospace.

[b]3. Balancing Stability and Growth Potential[/b]

The portfolio aims at balancing stability and growth by investing in established global defense firms as well as innovative technology-driven firms. Established defense firms provide stability with government contracts, while innovative technology firms provide higher growth prospects. This will enable the portfolio to increase its long-term return while maintaining an acceptable level of risk.

[b]4. Maintaining Risk-Conscious Portfolio Allocation[/b]

Considering the geopolitical, regulatory, and policy-sensitive nature of the aerospace and defense industry, the portfolio focuses on disciplined risk management. The exposure of the portfolio to the aerospace and defense industry will not exceed 30% of the total portfolio. This is to avoid concentration risk.

sections.title: Core Strategic Directions
sections.body:
[b]1) Selecting Companies with Proven Crisis Management in Governance[/b]

We focus on evaluating companies’ responses to crises and the transparency of their decision-making structures. Both qualitative and quantitative analyses are conducted on governance factors such as board independence, internal control systems, conflict-of-interest prevention, and shareholder rights protection mechanisms, with active integration into investment decisions.

We favor companies that have demonstrated fair decision-making and accountable management during exceptional crisis situations.


[b]2) Implementing an ESG Scoring System with Greater Weight on Governance (G)[/b]

While maintaining our existing integrated ESG analysis framework, we will increase the weighting assigned to the Governance (G) component.

A multi-layered governance assessment will be adopted, incorporating data from corporate governance reports, regular disclosures, general meeting agendas, CEO risk profiles, and whistleblower history.


[b]3) Excluding Companies with Governance Risks that Exacerbate Crises[/b]

Companies showing persistent audit opinion issues, controlling shareholder abuse, excessive executive compensation, golden parachutes, or obstruction of shareholder meetings will be explicitly excluded from investment consideration.


This strategy combines “insight to identify opportunities within crises” with “analytical capability for structural sustainability.”

By maintaining the broad ESG framework but applying more stringent governance criteria and analysis, the fund will establish a robust risk management foundation, enabling consistent performance even in unpredictable future environments.

sections.title: Governance-Centered Investment Evaluation Criteria

[ul][li]Over the past year, has the company responded to crises (e.g., performance downturns, industry recessions, regulatory changes) in a transparent and consistent manner?[/li]
[li]Were management’s accountability and decision-making rationale clearly disclosed?[/li]
[li]In exceptional circumstances, did the board of directors sufficiently explain its decisions through post-disclosure or investor relations (IR) communications?[/li][/ul]

[b]② Board of Directors and Internal Controls[/b]
[ul][li]Independence of the board (≥ 50% outside directors)[/li]
[li]Existence and effective operation of audit committees or equivalent bodies[/li]
[li]Operation of a whistleblower system and records of actual whistleblowing cases (including case count and content analysis)[/li][/ul]

[b]③ CEO and Controlling Shareholder Risk[/b]
[ul][li]Potential conflicts of interest involving the CEO (e.g., concurrent positions, related-party transactions with subsidiaries)[/li]
[li]Discrepancy between executive compensation and corporate performance[/li]
[li]Existence of golden parachutes or irregular shareholder meeting practices[/li][/ul]

[b]④ Treasury Shares and Shareholder Policy[/b]
[ul][li]Is the proportion of treasury shares excessive? (calculated as holdings relative to market capitalization)[/li]
[li]Potential use of treasury shares for management entrenchment[/li]

sections.title: Mission
sections.body: I seek to generate consistent, high-yield returns within a 1–2 year investment horizon while maintaining disciplined risk management. Using a data-driven investment strategy, I identify and invest in financially strong, high-potential companies that meet strict quantitative benchmarks before assessing their long-term stability and growth potential.

sections.title: Investment Philosophy
sections.body:
My approach is built on rigorous financial analysis, sector diversification, and risk-aware decision-making. I follow these principles:

[ul][li]Numbers-First Selection – Companies are first screened based on objective financial metrics, such as P/E ratio, revenue growth, profit margins, and debt levels, ensuring they meet or exceed industry standards.[/li]
[li]Diversification for Stability – The portfolio is balanced across multiple sectors to mitigate industry-specific risks and enhance resilience.[/li]
[li]Avoiding Speculation – We do not engage in high-risk speculative investments, including penny stocks or highly volatile assets, prioritizing stability and consistent growth instead.[/li]
[li]Profitability & Growth Potential – After passing quantitative screening, companies are further evaluated based on market position, competitive edge, and long-term expansion prospects.[/li]
[li]Responsible Investing – While ESG is not a primary selection factor, companies that directly harm the environment (e.g., excessive pollution, unsustainable practices) are excluded from the portfolio.[/li][/ul]

sections.title: Investment Strategy
sections.body:
To maximize returns while controlling risk, I structure my portfolio as follow:
[ul][li]50% Large-Cap Blue-Chip Stocks – Established, stable companies with strong earnings.[/li]
[li]30% Mid-Cap Growth Stocks – High-potential firms with proven expansion strategies.[/li]
[li]20% Small-Cap High-Growth Stocks – Emerging companies with solid fundamentals and strong profitability.[/li][/ul]

[b]Risk Management[/b]
[ul][li]Sector Diversification: No more than 20% allocation to any single industry to reduce exposure to market downturns.[/li]
[li]Stop-Loss Mechanisms: Implemented to limit downside risk and protect investor capital.[/li]
[li]Quarterly Portfolio Reviews: Performance is reassessed every three months, replacing underperforming stocks and rebalancing as needed.[/li][/ul]

[b]My Commitment to Growth[/b]
I focus on transparency, discipline, and strategic investment practices. By combining data-driven stock selection with strong risk management, I aim to outperform the market while maintaining a balanced and sustainable approach.

sections.title: Investment Philosophy
sections.body:
Our fund’s investment philosophy is to always seek opportunities amid economic and environmental crises. For instance, the COVID-19 pandemic, despite its disruptive impact on economies and societies, created unique and advantageous conditions for investment. Early in the pandemic, markets crashed significantly as uncertainty spiked. Many high-quality stocks and assets were heavily discounted, providing investors with "buy low" opportunities. Additionally, in response to the crisis, numerous emerging start-ups with high potential began to flourish. Recognizing these trends, our fund is committed to delving deeper into the challenges the world faces—whether major or seemingly minor—seeking investment opportunities that arise from them.

Another key factor influencing our investment decisions is ESG—environmental, social, and governance criteria. We believe that even highly profitable companies cannot sustain long-term success without aligning with ESG standards. As long-term investors, we prioritize ESG factors, with a particular emphasis on the environmental aspect, and assess them with a sophisticated approach.

In summary, our current focus is on climate change—an urgent global crisis that all nations must address. By exploring innovative solutions such as fuel cells, renewable energy, and eco-friendly business models, we aim to identify opportunities within this challenge.

sections.title: Investment Criteria
sections.body:
Qualitative Criteria

[ul][li]News and Public Awareness[/li]
[ul][li]Measure the frequency of mentions in news articles using Google Trends.[/li]
[li]Identify links between ESG factors and investment opportunities.[/li][/ul]
[li]Crisis Assessment (Disease-Related Investments)[/li]
[ul][li]Reference the WHO’s official statements to determine the severity of a disease-related crisis.[/li]
[li]Categorize severity levels based on WHO’s pandemic classification:[/li]
[ul][li]Asymptomatic/Pre-Symptomatic: No visible symptoms.[/li]
[li]Mild Cases: Minor symptoms, no hospitalization required.[/li]
[li]Moderate Cases: Symptoms require medical attention but not intensive care.[/li]
[li]Severe Cases: Serious symptoms requiring hospitalization.[/li]
[li]Critical Cases: Life-threatening illness requiring intensive care.[/li][/ul][/ul]
[li]ESG Evaluation[/li]
[ul][li]Analyze the company’s balance sheet to assess financial success in ESG management.[/li]
[li]Review the company’s environmental sustainability stance and commitments.[/li]
[li]Conduct research on internal corporate complexity, focusing on stakeholder dynamics.[/li]
[ul][li]Example: Korea Zinc has a vulnerable internal structure, making it a risk factor.[/li][/ul][/ul]
[li]Scientific and Technological Relevance[/li]
[ul][li]Study scientific literature on environmental sustainability.[/li]
[li]Focus on specific products and innovations that drive sustainable investment opportunities.[/li]
[ul][li]Example: Catalysts are essential for fuel cells, making investments in catalyst suppliers a strong long-term strategy.[/li][/ul][/ul][/ul]

Quantitative Criteria

[ul][li]Sustainability Measurement[/li]
[ul][li]Analyze the company’s balance sheet to assess net income/loss.[/li]
[li]Track financial trends over time to evaluate long-term stability.[/li][/ul]
[li]Market Trend Analysis[/li]
[ul][li]Utilize Google Trends to monitor public interest and industry momentum.[/li][/ul][/ul]

By combining qualitative insights (market perception, ESG impact, and scientific relevance) with quantitative data (financial performance and trend analysis), this framework ensures strategic and informed investment decisions.

sections.title: Investment Objectives
sections.body:
[b]1. Value-Based Investment Strategy[/b]: 

The investment strategy utilizes the Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio as a key indicator to identify undervalued stocks in the market. By focusing on companies with low P/E ratios, the strategy aims to capture long-term capital appreciation, providing investors with stable returns.


[b]2. Maximizing Dividend Income[/b]: 

The strategy emphasizes companies with high Dividend Yields to ensure a steady cash flow. Investing in companies with substantial dividend payouts not only secures dividend income but also benefits from potential capital gains. This approach targets stable investment returns through high dividend yields.


[b]3. Ensuring Financial Stability[/b]: 

Financial health is assessed using the Debt-to-Equity Ratio (DER) and Current Ratio. By selecting companies with low debt ratios and adequate current ratios, the strategy aims to strengthen financial stability and minimize risks during economic downturns.


[b]4. Enhancing Capital Efficiency[/b]: 

The Return on Equity (ROE) is used to evaluate how effectively a company utilizes its capital. By investing in companies with high ROE, the strategy seeks to maximize capital efficiency and assess the company's growth potential and profitability, thereby improving overall portfolio performance.

keyFeatures:
[b]Value Assessment-Based Investment[/b]: 

The strategy employs the P/E Ratio to perform relative value assessments of companies, focusing on those that appear undervalued. This approach aims to exploit potential value increases and capitalize on long-term growth prospects of undervalued assets.

[b]Stable Dividend Strategy[/b]: 

The investment strategy targets companies with high Dividend Yields to secure reliable dividend income. High dividend yield investments are selected to ensure a stable cash flow and to complement financial stability considerations in the investment approach.

[b]Financial Health Analysis[/b]: 

The Debt-to-Equity Ratio and Current Ratio are used to scrutinize the financial condition of companies. Investing in companies with low debt and suitable current ratios aims to reduce financial risks and create a financially sound investment environment.

[b]Efficient Capital Utilization[/b]: 

ROE is utilized to assess capital efficiency, focusing on companies that demonstrate high ROE. This approach seeks to enhance capital utilization and evaluate the company’s profitability and growth potential, thereby boosting long-term returns.

[b]Conservative Evaluation Approach[/b]: 

Trailing P/E (historical P/E Ratio) is preferred over Forward P/E to ensure a conservative evaluation method. Using Trailing P/E provides a stable basis for investment decisions based on past performance and helps manage potential risks effectively.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.body:
This Privacy Policy explains what information Youth Impact Fund ("YIF", "we", "us") collects when you use this website, how we use it, and the choices you have. YIF is a student-run organization based in the Republic of Korea.

[h]1. Information we collect[/h]
[b]Account information.[/b] When you create an account we collect your name, email address and a password. Passwords are handled by Google Firebase Authentication and are never visible to us. If you sign in with Google, we receive your name, email address and Google account ID from Google.

[b]Petition signatures.[/b] When you sign a petition we collect the name and email address you enter. If you are logged in, we also link the signature to your account.

[b]Votes, likes and comments.[/b] When you vote on a report, like a lesson or post a comment, we store your choice or text together with your account ID. Comments are shown publicly with your name.

[b]Technical information.[/b] Your browser stores a small amount of data on your device (local storage) to keep you logged in and to remember which petitions you have signed. Our hosting and service providers may automatically log technical data such as your IP address, browser type and the time of your visit.

We do not collect payment information, and we do not use advertising or tracking cookies.

[h]2. How we use your information[/h]
[ul][li]To create and manage your account and let you log in.[/li][li]To count petition signatures and make sure each person signs only once.[/li][li]To record report votes (one per member) and show lesson likes and comments.[/li][li]To reply to you when you contact us, and to send account emails you request, such as password resets.[/li][li]To keep the website secure and prevent abuse.[/li][/ul]

[h]3. What is shown publicly[/h]
[ul][li]Petition pages show only the total number of signatures. Signers' names and email addresses are not shown on the website.[/li][li]Report vote results are shown as totals and percentages, not by member.[/li][li]Lesson comments are shown with the commenter's name.[/li][/ul]

[h]4. When we share information[/h]
We do not sell or rent your personal information. We share it only in these cases:
[ul][li][b]Petition recipients.[/b] When a petition is delivered, we may share signers' names (never email addresses) with the company, organization or public authority the petition is addressed to.[/li][li][b]Service providers.[/b] We use Google Firebase (Google LLC) for accounts and data storage, GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc.) to host the website, Google Fonts for typefaces, and Google Drive to host report files and lesson videos. These providers process data on our behalf and may store it on servers outside Korea.[/li][li][b]Legal reasons.[/b] If required by law or to protect the safety of our members or the public.[/li][/ul]

[h]5. How long we keep information[/h]
[ul][li]Account information is kept until you delete your account.[/li][li]Petition signatures are kept while the campaign is active and for up to 12 months after it ends, then deleted.[/li][li]Votes, likes and comments are kept while your account exists. You can delete your own comments at any time.[/li][/ul]

[h]6. Your choices and rights[/h]
[ul][li][b]Edit your name:[/b] open your profile from the account menu.[/li][li][b]Delete your account:[/b] open your profile and choose Delete account. This permanently removes your login. Comments you posted stay unless you delete them first or ask us to remove them.[/li][li][b]Other requests:[/b] you can ask us to access, correct or delete your information, including a petition signature, by contacting us at {{contact}}.[/li][/ul]

[h]7. Children and young people[/h]
Many YIF members are students. If you are under 14, you need permission from a parent or legal guardian before you create an account or sign a petition. If we learn that we collected information from a child under 14 without that permission, we will delete it.

[h]8. Security[/h]
We use Firebase security rules to limit who can read and change data. For example, petition signatures can only be read by YIF administrators. No online service is completely secure, so please use a strong, unique password.

[h]9. Changes to this policy[/h]
If we change this policy, we will update the date at the top of this page. If the changes are significant, we will post a notice on the website.

[h]10. Contact[/h]
Questions about this policy or your information can be sent to {{contact}}.
